chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the slave slanders the free man, he is whipped eighty (lashes).
And he (peace be upon him) said: This is from the rights of the people.

key_terms.قَذَفَ: Slandered / Conferred illegitimacy (specifically in the context of hadd al-ridud)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a slave who slanders a free man in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that a slave who commits *li'an* (slander) against a free man is subject to eighty lashes, a reduction from the hundred lashes prescribed for free men. By categorizing this penalty as *huquq al-nas* (rights of the people), the Imam highlights its civil nature, implying that the victim may forgive or commute the punishment, unlike *hudud* strictly for God's sake. This distinction is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for understanding the flexibility of penal codes regarding social status and individual rights.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Iibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the slave slanders the free, he would be whipped eighty (lashes)’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is from the rights of the people’.
